# Quantum Training Robustness

> A scientific account of when finite pure-state training probes control the Haar-average error of a learned quantum operation, and the optimal certification cost under fresh inputs selected by classical labels.

The target is unitary; the hypothesis is an arbitrary CPTP channel unless a page explicitly adds a unital or exact tensor-product promise. The repository contains derivations, primary-source attribution, and reproducible finite numerical checks.

## Entry points

- [README](README.md): Main question, results, scope, purpose, and contact.
- [Scientific map](science/README.md): Reading routes and notation.
- [Interpretation](science/interpretation.md): Consequences for training, physical promises, and resource accounting.

## Definitions and proofs

- [Model](science/model.md): Pure probes, survival loss, Haar risk, and certification access.
- [Robustness](science/robustness.md): Exact Kraus identities; the common right-eigenoperator criterion; optimal linear coefficient; physical sharpness; full exponent trichotomy.
- [Probe geometry](science/probe_geometry.md): Coordinate-support graph, minimal support, explicit qubit obstruction, dimension dependence, and optimized basis-plus-superposition weights.
- [Optimal design](science/optimal_design.md): Universal support-size bound for arbitrary weights and imbalance, ETF equality conditions, and the projective 2-design endpoint.
- [Nonunitality](science/nonunitality.md): Exact commutator identity, sharp unital coefficient, quantitative deviation bound, joint frontier, and dissipative realization.
- [Certification](science/certification.md): Adaptive classical-to-quantum fidelity converse, minimax adversary, finite-sample sandwich, exact joint limiting coefficient, target-copy comparison, and noisy-baseline limits.
- [Product channels](science/product_channels.md): Exact tensor-product promise, uniform two-versus-three global probe laws, sharp coefficients, and physical costs.

## Interpretation constraints

Read the model before transferring a theorem to another access setting. R and R_H denote the same Haar-average infidelity. State fidelity in the certification proof is squared Uhlmann fidelity.

The variance gap is minimized over all traceless complex operators, including nonnormal ones. Restricting it to Hermitian operators removes the relevant dissipative directions.

Exact identification, finite-loss robustness, and statistical certification are different properties. The best global linear coefficient does not determine the full finite-error frontier.

The exact sampling coefficient for a fixed menu holds as both target error and decision error tend to zero, with system dimension fixed and ideal target-output projectors. Fixed-confidence two-sided testing has a bracket; perfect completeness has a sharper coefficient statement.

The adaptive lower bounds allow quantum output memory and collective readout, but each input is fresh and chosen by a classical label. The proofs do not grant input entanglement with retained memory, coherent probe choice, output recycling, or environment access.

The product-channel application requires exact tensor factorization. Every global example includes all n qubits and local channel uses. Its uniform scaling is proved separately from the fixed-dimension general theorem.

Training-loss estimates used to select a hypothesis are not automatically valid fresh certification data. Finite numerical checks corroborate constructions; they do not prove universal theorems or literature priority.
